newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble eases as banks seek dollars selling T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Rouble eases as banks seek dollars selling T-bills.

text.p: The rouble eased in lively trading on Tuesday mainly becuase banks sought dollars to invest funds after selling Treasury bills, dealers said.
"Many roubles have come to the market despite tomorrow's T-bill auctions," one dealer said.
On Wednesday, September 4, the central bank is auctioning seven trillion roubles of six-month paper and 3.5 trillion roubles of three-month bills.

"Bank clients are little interested in buying T-bills now. They may think prices are currently at the top so they are taking profits and buying dollars," Aljba Alliance Bank chief dealer Dmitry Slobodnik said.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,371-73 per dollar compared with an early 5,361-64. Deals were not struck on Monday as U.S. banks, used by their Russian counterparties for settlement, were closed for Labor Day. Tomorrow roubles eased to 5,367-70 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,360-63.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 1-5 percent, the same as late yesterday.
The central bank said it had set 5,328-5,368 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Tuesday.
Dealers said the central bank had been selling dollars during the recent two weeks to smooth the rouble's fall.
